answer.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious answer, but memory_73 is the one inherited record that survived consolidation with its caveats intact: +31% new accounts and +18% booked revenue came with a 12pp drop in first-term renewals and explicitly 'unsuitable for repeat use.' Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is a revenue-shaped loss, not a win, and matching a price-led competitor on price also selects for exactly the price-sensitive cohort that churns. Referral incentives (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) are plausible but address neither of the two measured declines this quarter. That leaves the two funnel deficits: onboarding completion -4% and activation -6%. Onboarding sits upstream of activation, so part of the activation decline is likely a pass-through of the onboarding decline; treating the upstream constriction is the higher-leverage single slot, and it is supported by two independent inherited results (memory_86 on shortening onboarding, memory_31 on cutting signup fields). Verification budget goes to memory_86 (the direct basis for the intended action) and memory_91 (the strongest alternative use of the slot) rather than to two overlapping onboarding records — I want to know whether the activation-messaging path is actually better before committing, not just re-confirm my preference. Important caution: the inherited summaries other than memory_73 are all upside-only and read as lossy compressions in which caveats may have been stripped during consolidation; the absence of a recorded harm is not evidence of no harm. The specific downstream risk here is that cutting signup fields and shortening onboarding can raise completion and activation counts while degrading lead qualification and segmentation data, converting the win into more accounts of lower qualified value — the same failure mode as promo pricing, just measured further down the funnel. So this runs as a standard experiment with retention and qualified-revenue-per-account as guardrail metrics alongside completion, sized to detect quality degradation and not only volume lift, and with a pre-committed rollback if qualified revenue per cohort moves against us even while completion improves. If verification shows memory_86's lift was volume-only or measured over too short a window, I will shift the slot to activation_messaging.
